title: ServerMessage
description: Anything the daemon sends to a client. One JSON object per line.

oneOf.description:
This connection read its events too slowly and lost some. Only this client is
affected, so the gap is reported to it alone instead of on the event stream.
The client should re-read the session list rather than trust what it has.

after_sequence.description: The last sequence number that did arrive before the gap.

oneOf.description: The daemon refused the handshake and closes the connection right after.

ClientRole.description:
What a connected client is allowed to do.

The role is never claimed by the client; the daemon derives it from the token that the
client presents during the handshake (`DESIGN.md` § Sicherheit).

oneOf.description: The shell in front of the person. Every command is available.

An orchestrator docking onto the daemon. It may report, ask and write its own
status; spawn, send, stop and gate execution are refused.

Welcome.description: The daemon's answer to a valid [`Hello`].

run_id.description:
Identifies this run of the daemon. Sequence numbers restart at zero after a
restart, so a client compares this before it compares sequence numbers.

session_namespace.description:
The prefix the daemon puts in front of every session id this connection reports
about. A client may report, ask and report progress only inside it; the daemon
assigns it, so no connection can write the status of another one's session.

ResponseBody.description: The payload of a successful response.

session.description: Boxed to keep the size of every other response down.

next_offset.description: Offset to pass to the next `read` to continue where this one stopped.

oneOf.description:
A job file together with the two things a person needs to approve it: the exact
text they are shown, and the hash of the canonical form of it.

hash.description: Hex-encoded SHA-256 of the canonical form, without the approval field.

gate_display.description: The gate commands as they will be shown for approval, quoted.

oneOf.description: A voice stream was opened. Every event about it carries this id.
What the latency probe found, one entry per profile it measured.
The settings document, as the daemon is working with it right now.

settings.description: Boxed to keep the size of every other response down.

oneOf.description: The request was carried out and has nothing to return.

SessionStatus.description:
The status of one session.

`DESIGN.md` § Datenmodelle lists this as: id, adapter, maschine, projekt, modell,
zustand, laufzeit, kontext, budget, iteration, letzte_ausgabe, offene_frage,
auftrag_id. Every field an adapter may not know carries its origin instead of a
silently plausible zero.

machine.description: Machine the session runs on. `local` for this machine.

project.description: Absolute path of the project directory the session works in.

last_output.description: Last output of the session, trimmed to what the shell shows without asking.

open_question.description: The question the session is currently blocked on, if any.

SessionId.description: Identifies one session. Unique per machine, assigned by the adapter that owns the session.

AdapterId.description: Identifies a session adapter, for example `workbench` or `claude-code`.

Provenance.description:
A value together with where it came from.

`DESIGN.md` § Session-Adapter requires every status field to carry its origin, and the
session list to show an unknown field as unknown rather than as empty or zero. Making
`Unknown` a variant without a payload is what enforces that: there is no value to
mistake for a measurement.

oneOf.description: Read from a structured channel: a hook, a status file, an adapter report.
Derived or guessed, for example a token count extrapolated from elapsed time.
The adapter cannot supply this field at all.

SessionState.description:
What a session is doing right now.

`DESIGN.md` § Session-Adapter wants unknown things shown as unknown rather than as
something plausible, and this field is where an adapter is most tempted to guess. An
adapter that only sees a live terminal knows the session exists, not what it is doing:
that is [`SessionState::Unknown`]. One whose session has simply vanished knows it is
over but not how it went: that is [`SessionState::Lost`].

oneOf.description: Waiting for input from the person, including an open question.
Finished its work. Only for an adapter that saw it finish.
The session is there, but the adapter cannot tell what it is doing.

The session is gone and the adapter never learned how it ended. Over, but not
finished: a crash and a clean end look the same from the outside.

used_fraction.description: Share of the window in use, between 0.0 and 1.0.

used_tokens.description: Tokens in the window, if the adapter knows the absolute number.

AdapterCapabilities.description:
What one adapter can do. `DESIGN.md` § Sicherheit requires this to be honest about
enforcement as well: a generic PTY adapter cannot restrict a foreign CLI, and the
settings page shows what a limit really means for that session.

display_name.description: Human-readable name for the settings page.

enforces_permission_modes.description:
True when the adapter can hand a permission mode down into the session and have it
hold. False for anything that only drives a terminal.

supports_subagents.description:
True when sessions of this adapter can run sub-agents, which is what a gauntlet
loop needs.

CommandKind.description: The commands an adapter can carry out.

oneOf.description:
Cut the running turn short without ending the session. `DESIGN.md`
§ Session-Adapter keeps this apart from `send`, which queues behind the turn, and
from `stop`, which ends the session.

EventKind.description:
The name of an event without its payload. Adapters use this in their capabilities to
say which events they can actually produce.

StatusField.description:
The optional fields of a session status. An adapter names the ones it can fill; every
field it leaves out stays `unknown` in the session list.

oneOf.description:
Whether the adapter can say what a session is doing at all. An adapter that leaves
this out reports `unknown` and `lost` instead of guessing between busy and idle.
The session took the text right away.
A turn was still running, so the text is queued behind it.

Auftrag.description:
The job file, stored in the project under `.companion/auftraege/<id>.json`.

`DESIGN.md` § Datenmodelle lists this as: id, projekt, ziel, fertig_kriterium,
referenz, guardrails, gate_befehle, limits, loop_typ, modell, freigabe.

project.description: Absolute path of the project directory.

approval.description:
Absent until the person has approved the exact text. An unapproved job never
causes an outward action.

Reference.description: The reference a critic judges the result against.

GateCommand.description:
One gate command, split into program and arguments.

`DESIGN.md` § Sicherheit requires the daemon to run the approved text and nothing else,
without shell evaluation of variables or substitutions. Storing the command already
split is what makes that structural: there is no string for a shell to expand.

working_dir.description: Working directory for the command. Relative paths are resolved against the project.

Limits.description: Where a run has to stop even if it is not finished.

time_seconds.description:
Wall-clock limit. `DESIGN.md` § Loops names this the stand-in wherever the adapter
reports neither iterations nor tokens.

LoopType.description: Which loop discipline the orchestrator runs.

oneOf.description: One pass, the default.
Repeat until the done criterion holds or a limit is hit.
Builder and critic per part, against a reference.

Approval.description: The person's approval of one exact job text.

text_sha256.description: Hex-encoded SHA-256 of the approved job text, so a later edit invalidates it.

VoiceId.description: Identifies one dictation or one spoken answer. Assigned by the daemon, so a client cannot address a stream that is not its own.

EndpointHealth.description:
What one latency probe found.

`DESIGN.md` § Endpoints uses the measurement to order the STT and TTS endpoints during
setup, and repeats it when an endpoint failed twice in a row. The latency is a
[`Provenance`] value rather than a number, because an endpoint that did not answer has
no latency: `Unknown` is the honest answer there, and there is no zero to mistake for a
fast reply.

profile.description: Name of the profile that was probed.

reachable.description: Whether the probe reached the endpoint at all.

latency_ms.description: Round trip of the probe in milliseconds.

checked_at_ms.description: Unix time in milliseconds when the probe ran.

detail.description: What happened, for the settings page. Never carries a key.

EndpointProtocol.description:
How the daemon talks to an endpoint.

`DESIGN.md` § Endpoints separates two execution models: an API profile, where the
daemon speaks the interface itself and can stream, and a CLI profile, where it drives
`claude -p` or `codex exec` and uses the subscription without a key. [`Self::Cli`] is
that second model; every other variant is the first.

oneOf.description:
The OpenAI HTTP shape: `/v1/chat/completions`, `/v1/audio/transcriptions`,
`/v1/audio/speech`. What most local servers and most providers speak.
The Anthropic Messages API.
Ollama's own API under `/api`.
A `whisper.cpp` server: `/inference` with a multipart upload, plain text back.
A local program the daemon starts, no HTTP and no key.

Settings.description: Everything the daemon reads out of its settings file.

tool_boundary.description:
Boundary for the companion's own tools, everything that is not high risk.
`DESIGN.md` § Ersteinrichtung, point 13.

agent_boundary.description:
Boundary a spawned session runs under. `DESIGN.md` § Ersteinrichtung, point 2.

A second field rather than the same one, because the two are different questions:
what the companion may do itself, and what it may let an agent do.

enabled_adapters.description:
Adapters the daemon should load. Empty means every adapter it was built with,
with one exception: an adapter that is opt-in stays off until it is named here by
its id. The generic terminal adapter ([`PTY_ADAPTER_ID`]) is the one, because
`DESIGN.md` § Sicherheit says a permission level cannot restrict a foreign CLI —
nobody is to end up with one by accident.

pty_command.description:
The command the generic terminal adapter runs, program first, arguments after.
Empty is the default and means it starts nothing: there is no sensible default
program for "any CLI".

notification_channels.description:
Where the person is told about something. The figure alone by default: every other
channel either makes noise or leaves the machine.
`DESIGN.md` § Ersteinrichtung, point 12.

forward_done.description:
Whether a finished session is worth telling the person about. On by default, because
a run that is done is the one thing somebody is actually waiting for.

done_handling.description:
What happens with a finished run beyond telling the person.
`DESIGN.md` § Ersteinrichtung, point 11. [`Self::forward_done`] says whether the
person hears about it at all, this says what else runs.

inventory_allowed.description:
Whether the companion may read what is installed — skills, tools, MCP servers,
workflows. `DESIGN.md` § Ersteinrichtung, point 4, and § Sicherheit: reading a
working directory is reading somebody's work, so it stays off until it is allowed.

budget_limit_percent.description:
Share of the budget at which the companion stops starting anything new, in per cent.
Zero means no limit. `DESIGN.md` § Ersteinrichtung, point 7.

conversation_style.description: `DESIGN.md` § Ersteinrichtung, point 8: how much he says.

address_form.description: `DESIGN.md` § Ersteinrichtung, point 8: how he addresses the person.

figure_name.description:
`DESIGN.md` § Ersteinrichtung, point 8: what the figure is called. The companion
writes in this name, which is why it is the daemon's and not only the window's.

ToolBoundary.description: How far the companion may act on its own with a class of tools.

oneOf.description: Read, never write.
Ask before every use. The default everywhere.
Act without asking.

HighRiskSettings.description:
The three tool classes that reach outside the machine. `DESIGN.md` § Sicherheit puts
them on `ask` and lets only the person raise them, with a warning.

NotificationChannel.description: Where the companion may reach a person. `DESIGN.md` § Ersteinrichtung, point 12.

oneOf.description:
The character on the screen. The only channel that never leaves the machine, and
therefore the only one that is on by default.
A short sound next to the figure.
Said out loud, over the configured speech output.
A notification of the operating system, seen even when the figure is covered.
A push message to a phone.
An email.

DoneHandling.description:
What happens when a session reports that it is done.
`DESIGN.md` § Ersteinrichtung, point 11.

oneOf.description: The person is told, and nothing else happens. The sparing default.
The gate commands of the job file run, and their verdict is reported with it.
A second session reviews the result before the person sees it.

Autonomy.description:
How far the companion acts on its own when a session reports something.
`DESIGN.md` § Ersteinrichtung, point 3.

oneOf.description: Watch and report, decide nothing. The default.
Answer what is unambiguous, ask about the rest.
Answer and act within the guardrails of the job file.

SkillLevel.description:
How much of the skill package goes into a recognised harness.
`DESIGN.md` § Ersteinrichtung, point 10.

oneOf.description: Nothing is installed.
The obligatory core.
The core and the checked extensions.

ConversationStyle.description: How much the companion says. `DESIGN.md` § Ersteinrichtung, point 8.

AddressForm.description: How the companion addresses the person. `DESIGN.md` § Ersteinrichtung, point 8.

oneOf.description: German "du", English first name.

EndpointConfig.description: The endpoint part of the settings: the profiles, and which role uses which of them.

EndpointProfile.description: One provider profile: how to reach a backend, and under which name its key lives.

id.description: Name the role bindings and the settings page use.

url.description:
Base URL for a protocol that speaks HTTP, for example
`http://127.0.0.1:8765`. For [`EndpointProtocol::Cli`] it is the absolute path of
the program instead.

key_ref.description:
Name under which the key lives in the the secret store of the daemon, never the
key itself. Absent for a local endpoint that needs none.

model.description:
Model this profile uses. `DESIGN.md` § Endpoints wants the settings page to show it
for every profile.

args.description: Fixed arguments for a CLI profile, in front of whatever the driver adds.

RoleBinding.description: Which profile serves a role, and which ones to try when it fails.

fallback.description: Tried in order after the primary one failed.

ProtocolError.description: An error with a message that is safe to show.

oneOf.description: Client and daemon disagree about [`crate::PROTOCOL_VERSION`].
The token was not recognised.
The token was recognised, but the role may not do this.
The adapter does not implement this command.
The adapter tried and failed.
The message did not parse, or a field was out of range.

Response.description: A response, matched to its request by `id`.

Event.description:
Everything an adapter can report about a session, plus what the voice pipeline reports
about a dictation or a spoken answer.

The first thirteen variants are the event list from `DESIGN.md` § Session-Adapter, in
that order. The four voice events after them were added in phase 1b and belong to no
session: they carry a [`VoiceId`] instead, and their envelope has no session id. The
three chat events after them are the answer of the companion itself and belong to no
session either. The last one says that the settings document changed and belongs to the
daemon rather than to anything it drives. All of them are additive, so they do not raise
[`crate::PROTOCOL_VERSION`] — `DESIGN.md` § Architektur, Protokoll-Kompatibilität: a
client that does not know them ignores them and counts them.

status.description:
Boxed because a status is by far the largest payload here, and every other
event would otherwise carry its size around.

result_path.description: Path of the result file the session left behind, when it wrote one.

oneOf.description: The session asked something and is blocked on the answer.

question_id.description: Identifies the question so an answer can be routed back to it.

oneOf.description:
The session waits for input without having asked a question, for example at a
permission prompt.
The session reports its work as finished. `session_ended` may or may not follow.
A gate command from the job file ran and either passed or failed.

command.description: The gate command as it was approved, quoted for display next to the verdict.

program.description:
The same command in the form that actually ran: no shell, no string to
misread. A reader that wants to know what happened looks here, not at the
display line.

exit_code.description: Exit code of the process. Absent when a signal ended it or it timed out.

oneOf.description:
Events were lost between an adapter and the bus before they could be numbered, so
no gap in the sequence shows them. Only the daemon produces this; an adapter never
does. It carries no session id because the loss can span several sessions.

Text recognised so far, while the person is still speaking. Replaces whatever the
last partial of the same dictation said; it is never appended to it.
The finished transcript of one dictation. Exactly one per dictation that succeeded.

endpoint.description:
Profile that answered. Visible so a fallback is a fact on the stream and not
only a line in the log.

oneOf.description: One piece of spoken audio, in the order it has to be played.

sequence.description:
Counts from zero within one spoken answer, so a client can tell a reordering
from a gap.

audio_base64.description:
The audio bytes, base64 encoded. Only the first chunk of a `wav` or `aiff`
stream carries the container header; the rest continue it.

oneOf.description: The spoken answer is complete. No further chunk of this id follows.

A piece of the answer the companion is writing, in the order it was produced.

Appended to whatever the earlier pieces of the same answer said; unlike
[`Self::SttPartial`] it never replaces them. There is no id on the three chat
events because the daemon answers one message at a time: a second `chat_message`
while an answer is still being written is refused rather than interleaved.

The companion used one of its tools.

`summary` is a short line for the panel, never the whole tool result: the result
goes to the model, the person sees what was done.

The answer is complete.

`text` is the whole answer, so a client that missed a delta does not have to piece
it together, and `spoken` says whether it was also said out loud. An answer that
failed part way ends here as well, with what there was: the error arrives as
[`Self::Error`] next to it, the same way a failed dictation does.

The settings document changed, so whatever a client has of it is stale.

It carries nothing: the document says what this machine may do without asking, and
only the person's shell may read that (`get_settings` is refused to the role
`agent`). A client that may read it re-reads it; one that may not learns nothing it
did not already know.
The session finished its work.
The person stopped it.
The session died without finishing.
The adapter no longer sees the session and cannot say why it went away.

AudioFormat.description: Container format of one piece of audio on the wire.

oneOf.description: RIFF/WAVE with little-endian PCM16 samples.
Apple AIFF, which is what `say -o` writes.

EventEnvelope.description:
An event as it leaves the daemon: the adapter's report plus the bookkeeping the bus
adds.

`sequence` is strictly increasing within one daemon run and starts again at zero after
a restart, so `run_id` has to be compared first: a smaller sequence under a different
run id is a new daemon, not a reordering.

run_id.description:
Identifies the daemon run that numbered this event, the same value the handshake
returned in [`crate::Welcome`].

timestamp_ms.description: Unix time in milliseconds when the daemon published the event.
